title: Model Context Protocol (2026-07-28) & Companion Web/Security Authorities

authorities.source: Model Context Protocol Specification (2026-07-28) — Authorization & Security Best Practices
authorities.rule_summary: MCP servers MUST NOT accept or forward client tokens upstream unless explicitly audience-scoped; upstream API credentials MUST be bound independently by the server.
Replaces stateful initialize handshakes with stateless server/discover capability metadata reporting protocolVersion 2026-07-28.

authorities.source: MCP SEP-2567 — Sessionless Streamable HTTP Transport
authorities.rule_summary: Eliminates sticky Mcp-Session-Id headers; every tool invocation MUST be self-contained with explicit pagination cursors and zero cross-request global state.

authorities.source: MCP SEP-2577 — Deprecation of Roots, Sampling, and Protocol-Level Logging
authorities.rule_summary: Servers targeting 2026-07-28 MUST NOT invoke client sampling (.sample()), workspace roots (.list_roots()), or protocol logging (.set_logging_level()).
Tools returning structured data SHOULD publish a valid JSON Schema 2020-12 outputSchema and emit matching structuredContent alongside backward-compatible TextContent.
stdout MUST carry exclusively newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages; all diagnostic and operational logs MUST be written to stderr.

authorities.source: MCP Streamable HTTP — x-mcp-header Parameter Mirroring
authorities.rule_summary: x-mcp-header annotations MUST apply only to non-sensitive primitive scalar fields and emit valid RFC 9110 header field-names without nullable anyOf unions.
Defines $ref resolution, allOf/oneOf/anyOf composition semantics, and schema validation rules adopted by OpenAPI 3.1 and MCP 2026-07-28.

authorities.source: IETF RFC 9700 — Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security (§4.14 Audience Restriction & Confused Deputy Prevention)
authorities.rule_summary: Resource servers MUST validate audience restriction and never replay bearer tokens across trust boundaries without explicit token exchange or separate server credentials.

authorities.source: IETF RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics (§5.1 Field Names / tchar)
authorities.rule_summary: HTTP header field-names MUST conform to token syntax 1*tchar and exclude CR/LF/whitespace/delimiters to prevent header injection.

authorities.source: IETF RFC 6901 — JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Pointer
authorities.rule_summary: Specifies deterministic fragment token escaping (~1 for '/', ~0 for '~') used in local OpenAPI/JSON Schema $ref pointers.

authorities.source: OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0 (§4.8.24 Schema Object & §4.8.30 Security Requirement Object)
authorities.rule_summary: Defines operation-level security overrides (including explicit unauthenticated security: []) and full JSON Schema 2020-12 alignment.

authorities.source: Saltzer & Schroeder (1975) — The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
authorities.rule_summary: Establishes Economy of Mechanism, Fail-Safe Defaults, Complete Mediation, and Least Privilege as foundational security engineering invariants.
